lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Faith, love and hope in Thessalonica
nodes.d: Paul thanks God for the Thessalonians' work of faith, labour of love and patience of hope, and recalls how they received the gospel and turned from idols to serve the living God and wait for his Son.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means that the Thessalonians turned from idols to serve the living God and wait for his Son (1:9-10)?
ev: Name the three things Paul remembers in 1:3
Describe how 1:9-10 sums up their conversion

nodes.d: Paul's first letter to the Thessalonian church, from thanksgiving for their faith (ch. 1) through his ministry and concern for them (2-3), to holy living, the Lord's coming and closing exhortations (4-5).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what 1 Thessalonians is about?
ev: Describe the movement: thanksgiving (1), ministry and Timothy (2-3), holy living and the Lord's coming (4-5)

nodes.d: Paul reminds them how he and his companions brought the gospel despite suffering at Philippi, working night and day, and treating them like a nurse and a father; the Thessalonians received it as the word of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Paul says he behaved among the Thessalonians and how they received the word (2:13)?
ev: Say why Paul did not flatter or seek glory (2:4-6)
Point out the nurse and father pictures (2:7, 2:11)

nodes.t: Longing to see them, and Timothy's report
nodes.d: Hindered from returning, Paul sent Timothy from Athens to strengthen them, and Timothy's good news of their faith and love comforted Paul and led to his prayer for their love and holiness at Christ's coming.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul sent Timothy and what news he brought back (3:5-6)?

nodes.d: God's will is their sanctification: sexual purity, not wronging a brother, brotherly love, quiet living and honest work.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by saying God has called us unto holiness, not uncleanness (4:7)?
ev: State what 4:3 says is the will of God

nodes.t: Those who sleep in Jesus and the Lord's coming
nodes.d: Paul comforts the Thessalonians about believers who have died: God will bring them with Jesus, the dead in Christ rise first, and all believers will be with the Lord for ever.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Paul says will happen to believers who have died when the Lord comes (4:16)?
ev: Explain why believers need not sorrow as those without hope (4:13-14)

nodes.t: The day of the Lord and living as children of the day
nodes.d: The day of the Lord comes as a thief in the night on those who say peace and safety, but believers, children of light, are to be watchful and sober, since God appointed them to salvation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says believers are not in darkness that the day should overtake them as a thief (5:4-5)?

nodes.d: Paul urges respect for leaders, care for the unruly and weak, joy, prayer and thanksgiving, testing everything, and prays that God sanctify them wholly and keep them blameless until Christ's coming.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three of the short commands in 5:16-22 and say why they matter?
ev: Describe how they are to treat the unruly, the feebleminded and the weak (5:14)

nodes.t: Persecution, God's righteous judgment and Christ revealed
nodes.d: Paul thanks God for their growing faith under persecution and says God will repay those who trouble them and give rest to believers when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says will happen when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven (1:7-10)?
ev: State what 1:6-7 says God will do for the troubled and for those who trouble them
Describe how Christ is revealed in 1:7-10

nodes.t: Timothy charged at Ephesus: sound teaching and the law
nodes.d: Paul left Timothy at Ephesus to charge some not to teach other doctrine or follow fables and endless genealogies; the aim of the commandment is love, and the law is good when used lawfully.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul left Timothy at Ephesus (1:3-5)?
ev: State the aim of the charge (1:5)
Explain how 1:8-11 says the law is used lawfully
